stem.text: A cell is described as having an electromotive force (e.m.f.) of $6\,\text{V}$.

A.text: 1 coulomb of charge always dissipates $6\,\text{J}$ of energy in the internal resistance of the cell.

B.text: 1 electron gains $6\,\text{J}$ of energy when passing through the cell.

C.text: There is a potential difference of $6\,\text{V}$ applied across any external circuit connected to the cell.

D.text: When 1 coulomb of charge passes through the cell, $6\,\text{J}$ of chemical energy is transformed.
